title: ring_scratch allocates on the heap via bare append and is never freed — its comment falsely claims it rides the temp arena
detail: Bare append on a zero [dynamic]u32 uses context.allocator (heap — no allocator swap exists in app/main.odin or harness/run.odin; only free_all(context.temp_allocator) runs per frame/tick), and ring_scratch is never deleted. Siblings take explicit allocators (growth_terminal_roster core/growth.odin:289 'alloc := context.temp_allocator'). Verified: odin test tracking allocator reports 6x 'leak 32B [growth.odin:526:growth_board_ring_scan()]' in test_growth_dublin_attach_stays_in_estate_radius. In a dublin app run this leaks one heap backing per growth window; the temp-arena comment is provably false.
recommended_fix: Allocate ring_scratch with an explicit temp allocator (e.g. make([dynamic]u32, 0, cap, context.temp_allocator) so appends inherit it) or add defer delete(ring_scratch); fix the comment to match.

title: map_board_destroy bad-frees when the board was arena-allocated — the new map tests load with context.temp_allocator then defer destroy
detail: Deleting temp-growing-arena allocations out of LIFO order is an invalid free. Verified: odin test tracking allocator reports 12x 'bad free [map.odin:136:map_board_destroy()]' in test_map_board_load_districts_parse and test_map_board_load_fail_loud_table — the only bad frees in the suite besides 2 pre-existing health_test ones. App/harness load on the heap so production is safe; the diff-introduced test pairing is not.
recommended_fix: In the tests, load boards with context.allocator (heap, matching app/harness) when deferring map_board_destroy, or drop the defer for temp-loaded boards; alternatively document the heap-only destroy contract on map_board_load.

title: json_get_int duplicates the existing jint helper in the same package, with silently narrower semantics
detail: package core already has jint (catalog.odin:1542) doing exactly this job, and it also handles json.Integer; json_get_int drops that case and would silently return the default for integer-typed JSON if ever reused. Same package — no import needed to reuse jint. Its own comment ('the catalog loader's convention') acknowledges the existing helper it redefines.
recommended_fix: Delete json_get_int and call jint (i32 def is fine for tile dims), or rename and justify the divergence; do not keep two same-package JSON int getters with different type-switch coverage.

title: strings_clone re-implements strings.clone from core:strings, which the package already imports
detail: The helper is byte-for-byte strings.clone (same default allocator parameter). core:strings is already imported elsewhere in package core (stats.odin:4), and map.odin could import it too — the 'self-contained' rationale duplicates stdlib code for zero gain.
recommended_fix: Delete strings_clone; import "core:strings" in map.odin and call strings.clone(attr, allocator) at the two call sites (lines 287, 320).

title: Dublin grid comment cites a nonexistent 'map.odin's GRID_ALPHA' and a stale 18% procedural grid rule
detail: No GRID_ALPHA symbol exists anywhere in app/render; the procedural grid is a 9% grid/91% canvas inline blend (grid_soft in view.odin map_draw) since the LEFOU pass. 46/255 (18%) matches the blessed gallery — the actual bar — so the code is defensible, but the comment's claimed parity with the procedural map's grid rule is false (and the constant it references does not exist).
recommended_fix: Reword the comment: the 46 alpha is the GALLERY's grid value (the KYLE-gate oracle), deliberately distinct from the procedural map's 9% canvas blend; drop the 'map.odin's GRID_ALPHA' reference.
